prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the depth map captures a dark, paved outdoor ground plane where the camera wearer starts with both arms extended forward in the lower foreground at 0.2–0.6 m in frames 1 and 2, with a wheeled cart or rack structure visible at the top-left edge roughly 3–4 m away. In frame 3, the wearer lowers their arms nearly out of view and turns right across the open ground (sloping smoothly from 1 m at the bottom to over 5 m at the top), before encountering a nearby person standing in red on the left at 0.5–1.0 m next to a tall wheeled cart or rack at 1.2–2.0 m in frame 4. By frame 5, as the wearer retreats or turns slightly, the foreground person is clearly resolved standing about 1.2–1.5 m ahead in right-side profile (facing right toward the cart within their arm's reach and not looking at the wearer), partially occluding the cart immediately to their right and a second person standing further behind them to the left at roughly 2.5–3.0 m (about 1.5 m behind the first person). The depth map reveals the silhouettes and relative distances of the two people, the cart, and the second person in the very dark frames 4 and 5 that are nearly invisible in the underexposed RGB image. However, the depth map looks unreliable in frame 3 where motion blur causes the lowered hands to vanish into the ground gradient, and in frame 4 where the close person and adjacent cart merge into a blurry, indistinct depth boundary.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's own left and right forearms in the lower foreground (at 0.2–0.6 m, spaced about 0.3 m apart) as separate masks in frames 1 and 2, detects nothing in frames 3 and 4, and segments the standing foreground person in the centre-left of frame 5 at roughly 1.2–1.5 m distance. In frame 5, the segmented person's silhouette is oriented in right-side profile facing toward the right side of the frame (away from the camera wearer's line of sight), with their head at the top edge and feet near the bottom edge. Compared to the dark RGB image in frame 5, this mask makes the foreground person's full-body contour and position immediately obvious against the dark pavement. However, the map is highly unreliable across the sequence: it splits the wearer's own two arms into separate 'person' instances and mislabels the right hand as an overlapping 'cat'/'person' ('catson') in frame 2, completely misses the blurred person and cart within 0.5–1.5 m in frame 4, and fails to segment both the background person at 2.5–3.0 m on the left and the wheeled carts in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons despite the presence of the camera wearer's extended hands at 0.2–0.6 m in frames 1 and 2 and two other people standing at roughly 0.5–3.0 m in frames 4 and 5. In the RGB and depth images, the wearer's hands are positioned in the lower foreground within arm's reach in the first two frames before dropping out of view in frame 3, while in frames 4 and 5 a foreground person stands at 0.5–1.5 m facing right with their hands near a wheeled cart and a second person stands behind them to the left at 2.5–3.0 m. Because no yellow body or magenta hand keypoints are rendered anywhere in the strip, this map provides no spatial information that is hard to see in the RGB image. The pose estimator is entirely unreliable in this sequence due to extreme low-light underexposure, truncated egocentric limb views in frames 1–2, and motion blur during the camera turn in frames 3–4.
